title: Approaches to marketing
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers the production, selling and marketing approaches; the closest ones are about general business ideas or management approaches, not marketing approaches.

draft.title: Approaches to marketing
card: The business focuses on making goods efficiently and cheaply. It assumes customers will buy what is available and affordable.
The business focuses on pushing the goods it has already made, using tools such as promotion and sales staff. It tries to persuade customers to buy.
The business starts with what customers want and then makes goods to meet those needs. Research comes before production.
The three approaches differ in where the business starts: with its products, with persuading buyers, or with the customer.
draft.remember: Production starts with making, selling with persuading, marketing with the customer.

a.q: Which business is using the marketing approach?
opts: It surveys customers, then designs a product to suit them
It cuts factory costs so that it can make more units
It hires extra sales staff to push its existing stock
It improves its machinery so that output rises each year
a.why: The marketing approach starts with what customers want, found through research, and then makes the product. The sales staff option is the selling approach, because it pushes stock already made.
a.clue: Which business begins with the customer, not the product?

b.q: Dan's bakery in Orange has a large stock of unsold fruit loaves. He trains staff to persuade every shopper to buy one and runs a big promotion. Which approach is Dan using?
b.why: Dan is pushing goods that are already made and trying to persuade people to buy them, which is the selling approach. It is not the marketing approach, because he has not found out what customers want before making the loaves.
b.clue: Were the loaves made after asking customers, or already made?

a.best: It surveys customers, then designs a product to suit them
